---
title: "Exchange rates"
---

```{ojs}
eur = await (await fetch("../data/fred/DEXUSEU.json")).json()
gbp = await (await fetch("../data/fred/DEXUSUK.json")).json()
broad = await (await fetch("../data/fred/DTWEXBGS.json")).json()
```

```{ojs}
viewof er_window = Inputs.range([2, 30], {value: 15, step: 1, label: "Years to display"})
```

```{ojs}
{
  const cutoff = new Date()
  cutoff.setFullYear(cutoff.getFullYear() - er_window)
  const filt = arr => arr.filter(d => new Date(d.date) >= cutoff).map(d => ({...d, date: new Date(d.date)}))
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 800, height: 320, marginLeft: 60, marginBottom: 50,
    x: {type: "utc"},
    y: {label: "USD/EUR ($ per €)", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(filt(eur.observations), {x: "date", y: "value", stroke: "#0e7c7b", strokeWidth: 1.8})
    ]
  })
}
```

{

```{ojs}
html`<div style="display: flex; gap: 0.8rem; flex-wrap: wrap; margin: 1rem 0;">
  ${[
    ["USD/EUR", eur.observations.at(-1)?.value, "$ per €"],
    ["USD/GBP", gbp.observations.at(-1)?.value, "$ per £"],
    ["Broad $ index", broad.observations.at(-1)?.value, "Jan 2006 = 100"]
  ].map(([label, v, units]) => `
    <div class="kpi-card">
      <div class="kpi-label">${label}</div>
      <div class="kpi-value">${v != null ? v.toFixed(3) : '—'}</div>
      <div class="kpi-sub">${units}</div>
    </div>
  `).join('')}
</div>`
```

## How to read

USD/EUR: dollars per euro. **Higher = euro stronger / dollar weaker.** A move from 1.05 to 1.20 is dollar depreciation against the euro.

USD/GBP: same convention. Higher means pound stronger.

Broad trade-weighted index: weighted basket of major U.S. trade partners, indexed to Jan 2006 = 100. Higher = stronger dollar against the basket. This is the cleanest single measure of dollar strength globally.

## What drives moves

Two main channels (PPP and capital-flow) work in opposite directions:

- **Higher U.S. inflation** relative to trading partners → dollar depreciates (PPP).
- **Higher U.S. interest rates** relative to trading partners → dollar appreciates (capital inflows).

In the short run, capital-flow dominance usually wins. In the long run, PPP usually wins. Watch both gradually.

## Source

[FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/) — DEXUSEU, DEXUSUK from the Federal Reserve Board's H.10 release. DTWEXBGS (Goods & Services trade-weighted index) is the Fed's preferred broad-dollar measure.
